summary: RAG anti-modal self-contrast: greedy anchor then regenerate
hypothesis: Showing the model its own greedy (most-generic) draft as a negative anchor and asking it to generate a fresh, superior set should push coverage out of the modal cluster — because the model's own output is the most relevant possible signal for what "generic" looks like on this exact task.
technique: A two-stage RAG pipeline: stage 1 generates a greedy modal draft (the model's most-confident, most-generic output); that draft is fed back as a dynamic negative anchor in stage 2, which generates a fresh 7 questions explicitly instructed to surpass it in specificity and coverage. Both stages use the same on-device model with RAG exemplars injected.
result: Scored 0.287 on dev-10 (0 wins / 0 ties / 10 losses vs Sonnet), down −0.036 from the exp011 best (0.323) and −0.020 from the baseline (0.307); discarded. Coverage stayed pinned at 3 — the model regenerated the same modal cluster verbatim, confirming that a dynamic self-anchor cannot substitute for the criticality judgment the 3B lacks, falsifying the hypothesis.
